protocol.name: river_window_scale_v1

description.summary: scale the rendered content of windows

protocol.description:
This protocol allows the river-window-management-v1 window manager to render a window smaller or larger than its actual dimensions, without the window knowing. The window is not asked to resize, the compositor scales the buffers the window has already rendered.
This is useful for overviews and zoom animations.

interface.name: river_window_scale_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.

entry.name: invalid_scale
entry.summary: the scale numerator or denominator is 0

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the river_window_scale_v1 object. Windows keep their current scale.

request.name: set_scale

description.summary: set the scale the window is rendered at

request.description:
Render the window, including its borders and decorations, scaled by numerator / denominator. The scale is relative to the top left corner of the window as set by river_node_v1.set_position. Clip boxes are given in unscaled window coordinates and are scaled with the window.
Popups of a window that is not at scale 1 are not rendered. The window does not receive pointer, touch or tablet input while it is not at scale 1, the input goes to the window manager as if it hit the window's borders. A window rendered fullscreen ignores its scale.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.
The initial scale is 1.

request.name: get_ghost

description.summary: keep the last frame of a window after it closes

request.description:
Create a ghost for the window. Nothing is shown while the window is open. When the window is closed, in the manage sequence that sends river_window_v1.closed, the ghost takes a copy of everything the window showed last: its buffers, borders and decorations, as they were rendered, including their scale and clip boxes. Popups are not copied.
The ghost is shown where the window was, on top of it, and stays until it is destroyed, so that the window manager can animate it away.
A ghost created for a window that is already closed, or whose window was not shown when it closed, stays empty. A second ghost for the same window replaces the first, which stays empty.

interface.name: river_window_ghost_v1

description.summary: the last frame of a closed window

interface.description: The requests of this interface modify rendering state. They are applied at the end of the next render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

entry.name: invalid_scale
entry.summary: the scale numerator or denominator is 0

entry.name: invalid_opacity
entry.summary: the opacity denominator is 0 or less than the numerator

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stop showing the ghost and free its copy of the window's buffers.

request.name: set_position

description.summary: set the position of the ghost

request.description: Set the position of the ghost's top left corner in the layout coordinate space, like river_node_v1.set_position does for the window. The initial position is the window's last position.

request.name: set_scale
request.description: Render the ghost scaled by numerator / denominator, relative to its top left corner and to the size the window was last rendered at. The initial scale is 1.

request.name: set_opacity

description.summary: set the opacity of the ghost

request.description: Render the ghost with its opacity multiplied by numerator / denominator, which must not be greater than 1. The initial opacity is 1.
